title: bug: `st.pyplot` crashes with an opaque PIL error for `format="pdf"`, `"eps"`, `"ps"`, `"svgz"`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`st.pyplot` forwards `**kwargs` to `savefig`, so `format=` accepts anything Matplotlib supports. But only raster output survives the image path. `format="svg"` was fixed in #16283; the remaining vector formats still fail, and they fail with an error from inside PIL that names neither the format nor a way forward.

`svgz` is the odd one out: it is simply gzipped SVG, so it is renderable in principle — the gzip magic bytes just aren't recognised as SVG and get handed to PIL instead.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import streamlit as st

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3])

st.pyplot(fig, format="pdf")   # UnidentifiedImageError
st.pyplot(fig, format="eps")   # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="ps")    # OSError
st.pyplot(fig, format="svgz")  # UnidentifiedImageError
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run an app containing any one of the four calls above.
2. The app raises from inside PIL rather than reporting anything about the format.

### Expected Behavior

- `svgz` should render, since it is gzipped SVG and SVG already renders.
- `pdf` / `eps` / `ps` cannot be rasterised without an external tool (Ghostscript or Poppler), which Streamlit does not bundle. These should fail with a clear message that names the format and points at `format="png"` or `format="svg"`.

### Current Behavior

Each format reaches PIL and raises there. Sniffing the buffer the way the current SVG check does shows why:

```
format  first bytes                        detected as SVG?  PIL result
png     b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n\x00\x00\x00\r'  False            OK
svg     b'<?xml versio'                     True             (bypasses PIL)
pdf     b'%PDF-1.4\n%\xac\xdc'              False            UnidentifiedImageError
eps     b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
ps      b'%!PS-Adobe-3'                     False            OSError
svgz    b'\x1f\x8b\x08\x00p\xf0xj\x02\xff'  False            UnidentifiedImageError
```

`svgz` starts with the gzip magic `\x1f\x8b`, so the existing `<svg` / `<?xml` check cannot see the SVG inside it. `eps` and `ps` share the `%!PS-Adobe-3` prefix, so they are indistinguishable by magic bytes and are both PostScript.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.
- [x] No, this is a new problem.

Not a regression — these formats have never worked. #16283 fixed `format="svg"` only; this is the remainder of the same class of bug.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (verified at `97eada51b4`)
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: macOS 15.5
- Matplotlib backend: Agg

### Additional Information

Related: #16283 (fixed `format="svg"`), #11489 (the original SVG crash report).

comments.body:
`st.pyplot` forwards `format=` to Matplotlib `savefig`, but after save only plain SVG is special-cased before the image path. In `lib/streamlit/elements/pyplot.py`, `marshall()` sniffs for `<svg` / `<?xml`…`<svg` and otherwise hands the buffer to `marshall_images` → PIL. That works for PNG/JPEG and for the SVG fix from #16283, but fails for `pdf`/`eps`/`ps` (opaque PIL/`OSError`) and for `svgz` (gzip magic `\x1f\x8b` hides the SVG). Expected fix: gunzip/`svgz` into the SVG path; reject unsupported vector formats with a clear error pointing at `png` or `svg`.

### Related Issues

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11489 — Same class of bug: `format="svg"` crashed in PIL because SVG bytes were treated as raster. Fixed by #16283; this issue covers the remaining formats.
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16283 — The SVG sniff/bypass that left `pdf`/`eps`/`ps`/`svgz` on the broken PIL path.

No open duplicates found; #9660 (`st.pyplot` cold-start render failures) is unrelated.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.5-high`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

A bit of additional context here: the kwargs support in `st.pyplot` is something that we have intended to deprecate (and eventually remove) for a long time. We also had kwargs support for `st.plotly`, `st.altair_chart`, and `st.vega_lite_chart`, but removed it last year. Pyplot is the least important chart type; that's why we haven't done this deprecation yet. But instead of fixing up these aspects, we should just deprecate it and remove it in a couple of months.

A couple of related metrics: only ~0.7% of all `st.pyplot` uses pass in custom kwargs, and there has been only a single usage of `format` within the last couple of days.

Closing per [USER]'s comment on the fix PR (#16430): kwargs support in `st.pyplot` is planned for deprecation, so extending it to non-raster `format=` values isn't the right path forward. The upcoming deprecation of `**kwargs` on `st.pyplot` will retire this whole class of bug.
